insight: The InboundGroupSessionData interface changed between matrix-js-sdk v34 and v38. The old version had `session_id`, `session_key`, `sender_key`, `forwarding_curve25519_key_chain`, and `keys_claimed` fields. The v38 version has `room_id`, `session`, `forwardingCurve25519KeyChain`, `keysClaimed?`, `untrusted?`, and `sharedHistory?` fields. The test data had to be updated to match the new shape.

matrix-js-sdk@38 on Node aborts (WASM `RuntimeError: unreachable`, exit 1) when `client.initRustCrypto()` is called with the SDK default `useIndexedDB:true`, because Node has no `indexedDB` global. This is a hard WASM abort, NOT a catchable JS exception: `try`/`catch`, `--unhandled-rejections`, and `NODE_OPTIONS` all fail to stop it. The fix is prevention, not handling: call `initRustCrypto({ useIndexedDB: false })` (in-memory store; works on Node but keys are NOT durable) and only when E2EE is explicitly opted in (`adapter.json encryption: true`, default false). Also: `createClient({ cryptoStore })` is legacy-crypto/migration-only in v38 — it does NOT persist Rust-crypto E2EE keys, so `SqliteCryptoStore` + `dataPath` does not make E2EE keys survive restart. Verified against the installed SDK (client.d.ts:91-96, 1104; client.js:1087).
